title: yadakchi.products.changed.v1
description:
The full renderable product. The largest payload in the system, deliberately.

Producers: catalog. Consumers: search, ops, web.
Kafka message key: product_uid — it must be set; compaction and partition ordering depend on it.
Cleanup: compact, retention infinite.

This file validates a whole Kafka message body: the shared envelope from docs/specs/02-EVENT-CONTRACTS.md plus this topic's payload. Unknown fields are ignored, never rejected, at both levels — that is what lets a producer add an optional field without breaking a consumer.

event_id.description: UUIDv4, unique per emission. Two emissions of the same fact carry different event_ids; consumers deduplicate on the payload's natural identity, not on this.

event_type.description: The topic name without the 'yadakchi.' prefix and without the version suffix.

version.description: Envelope and payload version. A removed field, a renamed field or a changed type is a breaking change: publish to .v2 and run both until consumers migrate.

occurred_at.description: When the fact happened, ISO-8601 UTC with Z. Consumers tolerate out-of-order delivery across partitions by comparing this, never by assuming global ordering.

producer.description: The service that emitted this message. Constrained to the producers declared for this topic in platform/kafka/topics.yml.

trace_id.description: Propagated across the whole chain for debugging. Minted by crawler on yadakchi.listings.observed.v1 and carried through every derived event; a service starting a chain of its own (a human admin edit, a scheduled recomputation) mints a fresh one. Every service logs it.

payload.description: search and web must never call back to catalog to render a result, so everything needed to render is here: the ordered offer list, all three vehicle status arrays, cross-reference equivalents and the downsampled price series. The payload never varies by user or vehicle — it must be globally cacheable. A tombstone — payload: null with the envelope intact — means this entity is deleted; compaction keeps it as the last word on the key.

product_uid.description: The cluster_uid minted by matcher, adopted unchanged. Assigned once, never changes.

slug.description: Persian, URL-safe, derived from the title plus a short identity suffix. May change when the title improves; old slugs still resolve.

title.description: Built from the representative member's title_normalized, never its raw_title — promotional junk here goes straight into the HTML title tag.

brand.description: Canonical brand key of the product, or null when the cluster has none.

authenticity_dominant.description: The modal authenticity claim across members. Prices differ ~4x across these grades, so comparing without the label is misleading.

part_numbers.description: Every part number seen on the members.

crossref_codes.description: Equivalent part numbers from other brands. A display hint only.

vehicles_incompatible.description: vehicle_slugs confirmed incompatible. Stored explicitly: search excludes only these, so that unmapped products stay visible.

vehicles_unknown.description: vehicle_slugs evaluated with no verdict. Shown with a caveat, never hidden.

risky_family_note_fa.description: Persian warning when this product belongs to a risky part family and the required granularity is missing. null otherwise.

offer_count.description: Number of active offers on this product.

min_price_toman.description: Lowest price across IN-STOCK offers only. The headline lowest price must never be a number nobody can buy. null when nothing is in stock.

max_price_toman.description: Highest price across in-stock offers only, or null.

median_price_toman.description: Median price across in-stock offers, or null.

offers.description: The ranked seller list, ordered by rank_position. Ranking is trust score first, then price — never purchasable. Out-of-stock offers are retained and labelled, never deleted.

offer_uid.description: The member offer this row denormalizes.

seller_name.description: The seller's display name, in Persian where they have one.

price_toman.description: Integer tomans, or null when the offer carries no usable price.

authenticity_claim.description: The seller's own claim for this offer.

trust_score.description: The seller's trust score at the time this list was built.

is_cheapest.description: Exactly one offer per product carries true, so the frontend can badge it even when trust-first ordering puts another seller first.

price_series.description: Downsampled daily price history, so web can draw the chart without a second call.

date.description: The day this point summarizes, YYYY-MM-DD.

is_published.description: true only with at least one active offer, a non-empty title and — for risky part families — an explicit verdict or the attached warning.

successor_product_uid.description: Set when this product was retired by a split or merge; drives 301 redirects. null while the product is live. A product is never deleted.
